title: Explain Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype, and when each is used.
shortTitle: Explain Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype, and when each is used
keyPoints: Factory Method picks one concrete product behind a method; caller never writes new.
Abstract Factory produces a whole matching family of related products through a factory interface.
Builder assembles a complex object step by step with chained setters and a build call.
Prototype creates a new object by copying an existing, pre-configured instance.
Factory and Abstract Factory answer which type to create; Builder and Prototype answer how to assemble or copy.
In modern Java, Factory Method often becomes a Map of Supplier, and Prototype uses a copy constructor.

s1_definition.oneliner: Factory Method picks one product, Abstract Factory picks a matching family, Builder assembles one complex product step by step, and Prototype copies an existing product.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Factory Method** – defines a method that decides which concrete class to instantiate; caller asks by key and never writes `new`.
- **Abstract Factory** – produces whole families of related objects that must be used together; swapping the factory swaps the entire family.
- **Builder** – constructs a complex object step by step through chained setters; the `build()` call validates and produces an immutable result.
- **Prototype** – creates new objects by cloning an existing instance rather than constructing from scratch.
- **Key distinction** – Factory and Abstract Factory answer which type to create; Builder and Prototype answer how a single object is assembled or copied.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, Factory Method is the single counter that hands Rajesh the right account-opening kit based on the type he asks for. Abstract Factory is the regional office that hands him a whole matching set: forms, card design, and cheque book for his region. Builder is how he fills a long loan application one field at a time and only submits when it is complete. Prototype is photocopying a standard pre-filled template form and tweaking a couple of fields instead of writing the whole form again.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Creational Patterns – What Each Solves
  ───────────────────────────────────────

  Factory Method:
  Client ──▶ Factory.create("EQUITY") ──▶ EquitySettlement
             (which one type?)

  Abstract Factory:
  Client ──▶ RegulatoryKitFactory ──▶ RegulatoryHeader
                                  ──▶ RegulatoryFormatter
             (which matching family?)

  Builder:
  Client ──▶ builder().tradeId().symbol().quantity().build()
             (step-by-step assembly → immutable result)

  Prototype:
  Template ──▶ template.copy() ──▶ independent deep copy
              (copy existing, tweak a few fields)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, and Prototype are four creational patterns, each solving a different construction problem.

Factory Method defines a single method that decides which concrete class to instantiate. Rajesh uses it at National Bank of India when picking an equity or FX settlement handler based on the trade type. It supports OCP because adding a new type means adding a class and one branch.

Abstract Factory goes a level higher and produces whole families of related objects. Pankaj uses it when generating documents: a regulatory filing needs a matching regulatory header and formatter, while a customer statement needs a friendly set. One factory hands back the entire matching family, and swapping the factory swaps everything.

Builder solves the telescoping-constructor problem. When a trade order has many fields, some optional, the Builder lets Rajesh set fields by name through chained calls and call `build()` to produce an immutable, validated object. Prototype creates a new object by cloning an existing one, which Rajesh uses for pre-configured order templates: copy the NSE template and tweak the symbol and quantity.

The senior point is that Factory and Abstract Factory answer which type to create, while Builder and Prototype answer how a single object is assembled or copied. In modern Java, Factory Method frequently becomes a `Map<String, Supplier>`, and Prototype uses a copy constructor rather than `Cloneable`.

Remember one sentence: Factory picks the type, Abstract Factory picks a family, Builder assembles step by step, and Prototype copies an existing template.
